name: subsignal-agreement-gate
rationale: The 2026-09-13 report's lead #4 is the sharpest diagnosis this pipeline has produced: measured over 15,248 candles, the composite signal never leaves [0.3359, 0.6548] and ta_normalized never leaves [0.2655, 0.7212]. The compression is NOT in the zone mapping or the TA/sentiment split -- both were verified structurally inert -- it is in the five-sub-signal weighted mean itself. That same report proved that merely dilating this curve buys turnover and nothing else: `ta-weight-085-signal-amplitude` scaled it by 1.2143x and lost 14.03 Sharpe. So the remaining question is whether the mean is averaging sub-signals that DISAGREE, in which case the narrow band is genuine cancellation and the resulting near-0.5 targets are noise being traded as if it were information. The 500,000 JPY baseline is consistent with exactly that: 771 trades at win rate 0.112 with a 384/387 buy/sell split is oscillation, not directional trading. This hypothesis does not change any sub-signal formula or any weight -- it requires CONSENSUS before the allocation may leave neutral, which is an information filter rather than a gain change, and is therefore not a repeat of the four weighting variants already tried (trend-weighted-subsignals, mean-reversion-weighted-subsignals, trend-weight-half, ta-weight-085-signal-amplitude), none of which can suppress a disagreeing point at all.
code_change_summary: Add a consensus requirement to the sub-signal aggregation inside TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs). This DOES touch compute_btc_target's body, which experiments/hypotheses/README.md permits on a dedicated worktree branch -- say so explicitly in your report. Keep every existing sub-signal formula byte-for-byte identical (RSI, damped SMA cross, damped EMA cross, damped MACD histogram, Bollinger %B), keep REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT = 1.0 and TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT = 0.25 unchanged, and keep the weighted-mean formula ta_normalized = sum(value*weight)/sum(weight) unchanged. Only add a gate AFTER ta_normalized is computed and BEFORE it is combined with sentiment_normalized. Define a named private constant AGREEMENT_MIN_FRACTION = 0.8 with a doc comment stating that it means 'at least 80% of the sub-signals this point actually supplied must agree on direction', that with the usual five sub-signals this is 4 of 5, and that 0.8 is an a priori round figure NOT fitted on any window. Also define AGREEMENT_NEUTRAL_EPSILON = 0.02 with a doc comment: a sub-signal within epsilon of 0.5 is counted as abstaining (neither bullish nor bearish) rather than being forced to a side by floating-point noise. Classify each of the sub_signals entries (use the raw value, IGNORING its family weight -- this is a count of opinions, not a weighted vote; say so in a comment) as bullish if value > 0.5 + epsilon, bearish if value < 0.5 - epsilon, abstaining otherwise. Let n_votes = bullish + bearish. If n_votes == 0, the gate passes trivially (nothing to disagree about). Otherwise require max(bullish, bearish) as f64 >= AGREEMENT_MIN_FRACTION * n_votes as f64, AND require that the majority side matches the direction of ta_normalized relative to 0.5 (a bullish majority with ta_normalized < 0.5, or vice versa, counts as failing the gate). When the gate FAILS, replace ta_normalized with exactly 0.5 -- neutral -- leaving everything downstream (the sentiment combine, the zone scaling, apply_zone, sticky_target, allocation_threshold, the lot-size check, the risk manager, the fee logic) completely untouched. When the gate PASSES, ta_normalized is used exactly as it is today. Because this lives inside compute_btc_target, both the live path and Simulator::run pick it up with no further wiring -- verify that is true rather than assuming it, and say so in your report. Add unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs's test module covering: all five sub-signals bullish (gate passes, value unchanged); 3 bullish / 2 bearish (gate fails, result is exactly 0.5 before the sentiment combine); 4 bullish / 1 bearish (gate passes); an IndicatorPoint supplying only RSI (n_votes == 1, gate passes trivially); every sub-signal within epsilon of 0.5 (n_votes == 0, gate passes trivially); and that the existing compute_btc_target_neutral_rsi_returns_some and compute_btc_target_warmup_all_none_returns_none tests still hold. In your report, state how many of the evaluated candles the gate rejected and the realized range of ta_normalized before and after -- the mechanism's behaviour, not just the report JSON -- and state explicitly whether the 50,000 JPY report differs from the baseline's at all.
constraints: This hypothesis DOES modify TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's body. That is permitted under experiments/hypotheses/README.md's '`compute_btc_target` may be modified' section, but ONLY on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch, and it MUST be reported explicitly so the coordinator flags it in any PR description.
MUST NOT change compute_btc_target's SIGNATURE. Only its body may change.

MUST NOT change any sub-signal formula, REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, the weighted-mean aggregation itself, the sentiment combine, apply_zone, sticky_target, allocation_delta_to_order, the lot-size check, the orders_below_min counting arm, the RiskManager call sequence, or the fee logic. The gate may only replace ta_normalized with 0.5; it may never move it anywhere else, and it may never enable an order the current logic would not have placed.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including every existing compute_btc_target_* unit test. Update an expected value only where the gate legitimately changes it, and do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass.

MUST NOT fit AGREEMENT_MIN_FRACTION or AGREEMENT_NEUTRAL_EPSILON on the holdout window, or on any window at all. They are a priori round numbers; if one turns out to be wrong, that is a result to report, not a value to retune mid-run.
MUST NOT change src/signal/engine.rs's broadcast cadence or anything about live scheduling.

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body and therefore changes the allocation target the live engine acts on.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the order-submission mechanics themselves.

paper_reference.title: Revisiting Ensemble Methods for Stock Trading and Crypto Trading Tasks at ACM ICAIF FinRL Contests 2023-2024
paper_reference.authors: Nikolaus Holzer, Keyi Wang, Kairong Xiao, Xiao-Yang Liu Yanglet
paper_reference.key_claim: On the Bitcoin task the ensemble aggregates its component agents' discrete actions by MAJORITY VOTE rather than by averaging, and reports a higher Sharpe ratio than any individual component (0.28 versus 0.15-0.21) while improving maximum drawdown by up to 4.17% on the equity task -- i.e. requiring agreement among components improved risk-adjusted performance more than it improved raw return.
paper_reference.pros: The mechanism is a pure aggregation rule over several disagreeing component signals, which is exactly shirube's structure (five sub-signals collapsed into one weighted mean) and needs no new indicator, no new config field, and no learned model to port. The paper's own framing -- that the ensemble's gain shows up in risk metrics rather than in return -- matches what shirube needs: the 500,000 JPY baseline's 771 trades at win rate 0.112 and a 384/387 buy/sell split is a risk/oscillation problem, not a return-forecasting one. It also models transaction costs and slippage, which most of the papers surveyed for this pipeline do not, and the crypto task is BTC.
paper_reference.cons: The components being voted on are deep-RL agents (DQN / Double DQN / Dueling DQN) over a learned action space, not rule-based TA indicators, so 'agreement' does not mean the same thing; the crypto result rests on only ~12 days of Bitcoin LOB data (7-19 April 2021) with no statistical significance testing, and the authors themselves note the agents may simply be converging because the action space is restricted, which would make the vote near-vacuous; the stock-side ensemble weights components by their VALIDATION Sharpe, a look-ahead-prone choice the paper does not defend; and the absolute numbers (Sharpe 0.28, return 0.66% over 12 days) are far too small a sample to transfer. Nothing from the paper is used as evidence here -- it motivates the mechanism only, and shirube's own 14-day holdout backtest decides, unconditionally.
